description.narrative: SummaryThe project is implemented in South Africa. The main outcome areas it contributes to are democracy and human rights, equality and worker´s rights and gender equality. The main rights holders are rural women, migrant women, small scale producers, farm workers and farm dwellers. Through trainings, study circles and dialogues the project aims to achieve progressive development within the outcome areas.Project OrganisationsThe project is a cooperation between TCOE and ABF Skaraborg, a branch of The Workers´Educational Association (ABF).Trust for Community Outreach and Education (TCOE) works with rural poor in Eastern Cape and Western Cape, especially regarding the right to and redistribution of land. TCOE also collaborates with a number of small agricultural organizations with a membership base of over 15,000 people in order to support their self-sufficiency and their political capabilities. As a result of its close cooperation with the agricultural collective, TCOE has established itself as a voice in the discussion on the design of the land reform and related policy.ABF is Sweden's largest adult education association. ABF offers study circles, courses, lectures and cultural events for about 750,000 people annually. ABF consists of 59 member organisations and 54 organisations within the Swedish labour movement.Other Donors to the OrganisationDonor funding linked to regional and national programmes from: DKA, NPA, CCFD, BCGMA, Bread for the world, Oxfam, Osisa, Fastenopfer, Apheda, AGS, AK, MOTT, Mama Cash, Southern Africa Trust.OPC will organise a donors meeting with Bread for the world and other donors in order to clarify which components and activities are funded by whom in order to complement each other rather than overlap, but also to make it easier for TCOE when reporting.Project ObjectiveTo deepen and consolidate the work done in the previous cycle: The well being and skills of rural women in the project have increased through the pedagogy of adult popular education and gained knowledge in recycling, agro-ecology and personal and organisational development.Actor groupsRights holders:Rural womenmigrant womensmall scale producersfarm workersfarm dwellersActor working in cooperation:institutions of higher learningtrade/ labour unions (CSAAWU)Mediaschools and churchesDecision Makers:Governmentparastatal institutions such as chapter 9 institutionsGender CommissionHuman Rights Commissiondepartment of Rural developmentdepartment of AgricultureMinistry of women, youth and persons with disabilitiestraditional leaderslocal authorities
